fields.description: Browser key for the Google Maps JavaScript API. Despite living in Travel Settings this is the shared desk maps key: the Travel Trip agenda map, the POI picker, the Pick Routing Map, and address autocomplete on the Address form all read it. In the Google Cloud console enable "Maps JavaScript API", "Places API (New)" (address autocomplete), "Geocoding API" (POI pins) and "Directions API" / "Routes API" (pick routing) for this key, and restrict it by HTTP referrer to your ERPNext domain(s). A missing API does not break the key — each feature degrades on its own, so an address field that never suggests anything usually means "Places API (New)" is off. Leave blank to fall back to a list of Google Maps links.
fields.label: Google Maps API Key

Google Geocoding API Key (server-side)
fields.description:
A SECOND key, for calls this server makes itself — currently the Geocoding API that turns a Project's address into site coordinates (workforce/sites.py), which is what the Time Kiosk's geofence measures against. It must exist separately because the key above is restricted by HTTP referrer, and Google refuses a referrer-restricted key on any server-side web-service call: it answers REQUEST_DENIED with “API keys with referer restrictions cannot be used with this API”. A browser key cannot be made to work here, and loosening the browser key's restriction to fix it would expose it.

In the Cloud Console create a key and restrict it TWO ways: by API to the “Geocoding API” only, and by IP address to this server's egress address (35.194.95.244). Not by referrer — that is what breaks it. This field is a Password: unlike the browser key it never leaves the server, so it is stored encrypted and is not readable through the API or a report view.

Leave blank to fall back to the browser key above, which preserves the old behaviour on a site that has not set this up — geocoding simply keeps failing with REQUEST_DENIED and is logged, never raised.

Use the newer Routes API (routes.Route.computeRoutes) for the Pick Routing Map instead of the deprecated DirectionsService. Requires "Routes API" enabled on the Cloud project AND added to this key's API restriction list -- that is a console change outside any deploy, so leave this off until it is done. When on, the map still falls back to DirectionsService automatically if a Routes call fails. Turn it off to stop using Routes immediately, without a deploy.
fields.label: Use Routes API (beta)
